imo-isl-2015-a1.prompt:
Suppose that a sequence $a_1, a_2, \dots$ of positive real numbers satisfies
$$a_{k+1} \ge \frac{k a_k}{a_k^2 + (k-1)}$$
for every positive integer $k$. Prove that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n \ge n$ for every $n \ge 2$.
imo-isl-2015-a1.answer: Rewrite the condition as $a_k \ge \frac{k}{a_{k+1}} - \frac{k-1}{a_k}$ and telescope to get $a_1+\dots+a_m \ge \frac{m}{a_{m+1}}$; then induct on $n$, splitting into $a_{n+1}\ge 1$ and $a_{n+1}<1$.

imo-isl-2015-a2.prompt:
Determine all functions $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ with the property that
$$f\big(x - f(y)\big) = f\big(f(x)\big) - f(y) - 1$$
holds for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}$.
imo-isl-2015-a2.answer: Exactly two: the constant function $f(x) = -1$ and the successor function $f(x) = x + 1$.

imo-isl-2015-a3.prompt:
Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. Find the maximum possible value of
$$\sum_{1 \le r < s \le 2n} (s - r - n)\, x_r x_s ,$$
where $-1 \le x_i \le 1$ for all $i = 1, 2, \dots, 2n$.

imo-isl-2015-a5.prompt:
Let $2\mathbb{Z}+1$ denote the set of odd integers. Find all functions $f:\mathbb{Z}\to 2\mathbb{Z}+1$ satisfying
$$f\big(x + f(x) + y\big) + f\big(x - f(x) - y\big) = f(x+y) + f(x-y)$$
for every $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}$.
imo-isl-2015-a5.answer: Fix an odd positive integer $d$, an integer $k$ and odd integers $\ell_0, \ell_1, \dots, \ell_{d-1}$; then $f(md + i) = 2kmd + \ell_i d$ ($m\in\mathbb Z$, $0\le i\le d-1$). These are exactly the solutions.

imo-isl-2015-a6.prompt:
Let $n$ be a fixed integer with $n \ge 2$. We say that two polynomials $P$ and $Q$ with real coefficients are *block-similar* if for each $i \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ the sequences
$$P(2015i),\ P(2015i - 1),\ \dots,\ P(2015i - 2014)\qquad\text{and}\qquad Q(2015i),\ Q(2015i - 1),\ \dots,\ Q(2015i - 2014)$$
are permutations of each other.

(a) Prove that there exist distinct block-similar polynomials of degree $n + 1$.

(b) Prove that there do not exist distinct block-similar polynomials of degree $n$.
imo-isl-2015-a6.answer: (a) $P(x)=T(x)=\prod_{i=0}^n(x-2015i)$ and $Q(x)=T(x-1)$. (b) Summation polynomials show $P-Q=\alpha\big(T(x)-T(x-1)\big)$ and $P+Q$ constant, reducing to $P$ block-similar to $-P$, which fails by a sign/size argument on the first block.

imo-isl-2015-c1.prompt:
In Lineland there are $n \ge 1$ towns, arranged along a road running from left to right. Each town has a *left bulldozer* (put to the left of the town and facing left) and a *right bulldozer* (put to the right of the town and facing right). The sizes of the $2n$ bulldozers are distinct. Every time when a right and a left bulldozer confront each other, the larger bulldozer pushes the smaller one off the road. On the other hand, the bulldozers are quite unprotected at their rears; so, if a bulldozer reaches the rear-end of another one, the first one pushes the second one off the road, regardless of their sizes.

Let $A$ and $B$ be two towns, with $B$ being to the right of $A$. We say that town $A$ can *sweep town $B$ away* if the right bulldozer of $A$ can move over to $B$ pushing off all bulldozers it meets. Similarly, $B$ can sweep $A$ away if the left bulldozer of $B$ can move to $A$ pushing off all bulldozers of all towns on its way.

Prove that there is exactly one town which cannot be swept away by any other one.
imo-isl-2015-c1.answer: Induct on $n$: the largest useful bulldozer, say the right bulldozer of $T_k$, sweeps away every town to its right, and those towns cannot sweep anything at or left of $T_k$; delete them and apply induction to $T_1,\dots,T_k$.

imo-isl-2015-c3.prompt: For a finite set $A$ of positive integers, we call a partition of $A$ into two disjoint nonempty subsets $A_1$ and $A_2$ *good* if the least common multiple of the elements in $A_1$ is equal to the greatest common divisor of the elements in $A_2$. Determine the minimum value of $n$ such that there exists a set of $n$ positive integers with exactly $2015$ good partitions.

imo-isl-2015-c4.prompt:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Two players $A$ and $B$ play a game in which they take turns choosing positive integers $k \le n$. The rules of the game are:

(i) A player cannot choose a number that has been chosen by either player on any previous turn.

(ii) A player cannot choose a number consecutive to any of those the player has already chosen on any previous turn.

(iii) The game is a draw if all numbers have been chosen; otherwise the player who cannot choose a number anymore loses the game.

The player $A$ takes the first turn. Determine the outcome of the game, assuming that both players use optimal strategies.
imo-isl-2015-c4.answer: The game is a draw for $n = 1, 2, 4, 6$; for all other $n$, player $B$ wins.

imo-isl-2015-c6.prompt: Let $S$ be a nonempty set of positive integers. We say that a positive integer $n$ is *clean* if it has a unique representation as a sum of an odd number of distinct elements from $S$. Prove that there exist infinitely many positive integers that are not clean.
imo-isl-2015-c6.answer: Assume all $n>N$ are clean. Then representations are unique, every large number also has a unique *even* representation, and the even representation of any large $t\in S$ contains every element of $S$ between $N$ and $t$; this forces a gap $s_{p+1}\ge 2s_p$, and the even representation of $2s_p$ yields a second odd representation of $s_p$.

imo-isl-2015-c7.prompt: In a company of people some pairs are enemies. A group of people is called *unsociable* if the number of members in the group is odd and at least $3$, and it is possible to arrange all its members around a round table so that every two neighbors are enemies. Given that there are at most $2015$ unsociable groups, prove that it is possible to partition the company into $11$ parts so that no two enemies are in the same part.
imo-isl-2015-c7.answer: A graph with chromatic number $k\ge3$ has at least $2^{k-1}-k$ odd cycles with different vertex sets: in a lexicographically minimal $k$-colouring, for each odd set $C$ of at least $3$ colours there is an odd cycle using exactly the colours in $C$. Since $2^{11}-12>2015$, the chromatic number is at most $11$.

imo-isl-2015-g1.prompt: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with orthocenter $H$. Let $G$ be the point such that the quadrilateral $ABGH$ is a parallelogram. Let $I$ be the point on the line $GH$ such that $AC$ bisects $HI$. Suppose that the line $AC$ intersects the circumcircle of the triangle $GCI$ at $C$ and $J$. Prove that $IJ = AH$.
imo-isl-2015-g1.answer: $BGCH$ is cyclic (right angles at $B$ and $H$), so $\angle CJI=\angle CGH=\angle CBH=\angle HAC$; with $M=AC\cap GH$ the midpoint of $HI$ and $D$ the reflection of $A$ across the foot of the perpendicular from $H$ to $AC$, triangles $IMJ$ and $HMD$ are congruent, so $IJ=HD=AH$.

imo-isl-2015-g3.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle C = 90^\circ$, and let $H$ be the foot of the altitude from $C$. A point $D$ is chosen inside the triangle $CBH$ so that $CH$ bisects $AD$. Let $P$ be the intersection point of the lines $BD$ and $CH$. Let $\omega$ be the semicircle with diameter $BD$ that meets the segment $CB$ at an interior point. A line through $P$ is tangent to $\omega$ at $Q$. Prove that the lines $CQ$ and $AD$ meet on $\omega$.
imo-isl-2015-g3.answer: With $K$, $L$ the projections of $D$ on $AB$ and of $Q$ on $DB$: $\frac{AH}{HB}=\frac{PD}{PB}=\frac{DL}{LB}$ (parallel lines and the bisector theorem, $QD$ bisecting $\angle PQL$), so the spiral similarity at $B$ taking $A\mapsto D$ takes $H\mapsto L$ and $C\mapsto Q$; then $\angle ADB=\angle CQB$ and the intersection of $AD$, $CQ$ lies on the circle $BDQ$.

imo-isl-2015-g4.prompt: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $AC$. A circle $\omega$ passing through $B$ and $M$ meets the sides $AB$ and $BC$ again at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $T$ be the point such that the quadrilateral $BPTQ$ is a parallelogram. Suppose that $T$ lies on the circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$. Determine all possible values of $BT/BM$.

imo-isl-2015-g5.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $CA \ne CB$. Let $D$, $F$, and $G$ be the midpoints of the sides $AB$, $AC$, and $BC$, respectively. A circle $\Gamma$ passing through $C$ and tangent to $AB$ at $D$ meets the segments $AF$ and $BG$ at $H$ and $I$, respectively. The points $H'$ and $I'$ are symmetric to $H$ and $I$ about $F$ and $G$, respectively. The line $H'I'$ meets $CD$ and $FG$ at $Q$ and $M$, respectively. The line $CM$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $P$. Prove that $CQ = QP$.
imo-isl-2015-g5.answer: With $R$, $S$ the second intersections of $DF$, $DG$ with $\Gamma$: powers of points show $H'I'GF$, $ADH'R$, $RSGF$ cyclic, so $R,S$ lie on $H'I'$ and $C,P,I',H'$ are concyclic; then $QH'\cdot QR=QC^2=QI'\cdot QS$, and the inversion at $Q$ with radius $QC$ swaps $\Gamma$ and the circle $CH'I'$, fixing $P$, so $QP=QC$.

imo-isl-2015-g7.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral, and let $P$, $Q$, $R$, and $S$ be points on the sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$, respectively. Let the line segments $PR$ and $QS$ meet at $O$. Suppose that each of the quadrilaterals $APOS$, $BQOP$, $CROQ$, and $DSOR$ has an incircle. Prove that the lines $AC$, $PQ$, and $RS$ are either concurrent or parallel to each other.
imo-isl-2015-g7.answer: By Menelaus it suffices to show $\frac{AP}{PB}\cdot\frac{BQ}{QC}\cdot\frac{CR}{RD}\cdot\frac{DS}{SA}=1$; this follows from the incenter identity $\frac{EF\cdot FG}{GH\cdot HE}=\frac{FM^2}{HM^2}$ for a tangential quadrilateral $EFGH$ with incenter $M$, applied to the four small quadrilaterals, together with similar right triangles formed by neighbouring incenters.

imo-isl-2015-g8.prompt:
A *triangulation* of a convex polygon $\Pi$ is a partitioning of $\Pi$ into triangles by diagonals having no common points other than the vertices of the polygon. We say that a triangulation is a *Thaiangulation* if all triangles in it have the same area.

Prove that any two different Thaiangulations of a convex polygon $\Pi$ differ by exactly two triangles. (In other words, prove that it is possible to replace one pair of triangles in the first Thaiangulation with a different pair of triangles so as to obtain the second Thaiangulation.)
imo-isl-2015-g8.answer: Key facts: a triangulation contains at most one parallelogram (two triangles forming a parallelogram), and every triangle of a Thaiangulation has a side on $\Pi$ (affine map to an equilateral triangle). Then a minimal counterexample, examined at an ear of one Thaiangulation, produces a triangulation with two parallelograms.

imo-isl-2015-n1.prompt: Determine all positive integers $M$ for which the sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$, defined by $a_0 = \dfrac{2M+1}{2}$ and $a_{k+1} = a_k\lfloor a_k\rfloor$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \dots$, contains at least one integer term.
imo-isl-2015-n1.answer: All integers $M \ge 2$ (for $M = 1$ the sequence is constantly $\frac32$).

imo-isl-2015-n2.prompt: Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers such that $a!\,b!$ is a multiple of $a! + b!$. Prove that $3a \ge 2b + 2$.
imo-isl-2015-n2.answer: For $a<b$ write $c=b-a$ and $M=\frac{b!}{a!}$; then $1+M \mid a!$, and coprimality with $c!$ (and with $c+1$ when $a=2c+1$) gives $1+M \mid (c+1)(c+2)\cdots a$. If $a\le 2c+1$, the right side is smaller than $M$, a contradiction; so $a\ge 2c+2$.

imo-isl-2015-n3.prompt: Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers such that $m > n$. Define $x_k = \dfrac{m+k}{n+k}$ for $k = 1, 2, \dots, n+1$. Prove that if all the numbers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{n+1}$ are integers, then $x_1x_2\cdots x_{n+1} - 1$ is divisible by an odd prime.
imo-isl-2015-n3.answer: With $a_k = x_k - 1 = \frac{m-n}{n+k}$: exactly one of $n+1,\dots,2n+1$ (namely $2^c$) has the maximal power of $2$. So all $a_k$ but one are divisible by $2^{d-c+1}$ while $P = \prod(a_k+1)-1 \equiv a_\ell \not\equiv 0$, yet $P \ge 2^{d-c+1}$; hence $P$ is not a power of $2$.

imo-isl-2015-n4.prompt:
Suppose that $a_0, a_1, \dots$ and $b_0, b_1, \dots$ are two sequences of positive integers satisfying $a_0, b_0 \ge 2$ and
$$a_{n+1} = \gcd(a_n, b_n) + 1,\qquad b_{n+1} = \operatorname{lcm}(a_n, b_n) - 1$$
for all $n \ge 0$. Prove that the sequence $(a_n)$ is eventually periodic; in other words, there exist integers $N \ge 0$ and $t > 0$ such that $a_{n+t} = a_n$ for all $n \ge N$.
imo-isl-2015-n4.answer: With $s_n = a_n + b_n$ and $w_n$ the least $m \ge a_n$ not dividing $s_n$, the sequence $(w_n)$ is non-increasing, hence eventually constant $= w$, and $g_n = \gcd(w, s_n)$ is then constant $= g$; so $(a_n)$ eventually cycles through $g+1, g+2, \dots, w$.

imo-isl-2015-n6.prompt:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ denote the set of positive integers. Consider a function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. For any $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ we write $f^n(m) = \underbrace{f(f(\dots f}_{n}(m)\dots))$. Suppose that $f$ has the following two properties:

(i) If $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, then $\dfrac{f^n(m) - m}{n} \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$;

(ii) The set $\mathbb{Z}_{>0} \setminus \{f(n) \mid n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}\}$ is finite.

Prove that the sequence $f(1) - 1,\ f(2) - 2,\ f(3) - 3,\ \dots$ is periodic.
imo-isl-2015-n6.answer: $f$ is injective with $f(m)>m$, so the positive integers split into finitely many chains $a_i, f(a_i), f^2(a_i),\dots$. A density/pigeonhole argument plus divisibility by $y-j$ shows every chain is an arithmetic progression (step $T_i$), and then $f(n+T)-(n+T)=f(n)-n$ with $T=\operatorname{lcm}(T_i)$.

imo-isl-2015-n7.prompt: Let $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ denote the set of positive integers. For any positive integer $k$, a function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ is called *$k$-good* if $\gcd\big(f(m) + n, f(n) + m\big) \le k$ for all $m \ne n$. Find all $k$ such that there exists a $k$-good function.
imo-isl-2015-n7.answer: Exactly the $k \ge 2$. No $1$-good function exists (a parity argument), and $f(n) = 2^{g(n)+1} - n - 1$ with $g(1) = 1$, $g(n+1) = \big(2^{g(n)+1}\big)!$ is $2$-good.

imo-isl-2015-n8.prompt:
For every positive integer $n$ with prime factorization $n = \prod_{i=1}^{k} p_i^{\alpha_i}$, define
$$\mho(n) = \sum_{i:\ p_i > 10^{100}} \alpha_i .$$
That is, $\mho(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ greater than $10^{100}$, counted with multiplicity.

Find all strictly increasing functions $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ such that
$$\mho\big(f(a) - f(b)\big) \le \mho(a - b)\quad\text{for all integers } a \text{ and } b \text{ with } a > b.$$
imo-isl-2015-n8.answer: $f(x) = ax + b$, where $b$ is any integer and $a$ is a positive integer with $\mho(a) = 0$ (no prime factor above $10^{100}$).
